problem: Multimodal language understanding methods for fetching instructions must score every (target candidate, destination candidate) pair, giving O(M*N) inference cost that is impractical for fetch-and-carry instructions containing two referring expressions.
motivation: Domestic service robots must resolve both the object to move and the destination from free-form instructions such as 'Move the bottle on the left side of the plate to the empty chair'. With about 100 candidates each, pairwise inference needs 10000 forward passes (about 40 s), which is too slow for a robot.
key_idea: Switching Head-Tail Funnel UNITER uses one model that zero-fills either the target or the destination input (Switching Head) and uses a mode-specific final FC layer (Switching Tail) to predict target and destination separately, cutting complexity to O(M+N).
insight: Sharing one model across the two modes with multi-task learning helps accuracy as well as speed. Removing the Switching Tail (single-task learning of each role in one model) drops accuracy by 6.2 points, and removing the Switching Head (duplicating the same input into both slots) drops it by 4.7 points. Error analysis shows the main bottleneck is serious comprehension errors, meaning weak visual-language grounding; the authors suggest pretrained models such as CLIP.
method: Input encoding: ResNet50 fc6 features (1024-d, from a Faster R-CNN backbone) with a 7-d box positional encoding for the target candidate, destination candidate and K detected regions; the instruction is tokenized with WordPiece.
Switching Head: in target mode the destination feature is zero-filled, and in destination mode the target feature is zero-filled, which conditions the model on what to predict.
Switching Image Embedder: separate FC layers plus normalization for the target, destination and detected-region features, concatenated as the image tokens.

Funnel Transformer: L=2 layers over the concatenated image and text tokens, with max-pooling applied to the query, key and value (the original applied it to the query only), halving hidden size and heads per layer.
Switching Tail: a mode-specific FC layer with softmax outputs p(y_targ) or p(y_dest), each binarized at 0.5; the final label is y_targ AND y_dest.
Multi-task loss: cross-entropy per mode with lambda_targ=lambda_dest=1, one term zeroed depending on the mode.

ALFRED-fc dataset: built from ALFRED Pick&Place sub-goals as image pairs taken before grasp and after place, with the target region masked in the destination image; positives have IoU>=0.7, negatives come from IoU<=0.3 regions, swapped instructions, or both.

setting.backbone: SHeFU (Funnel Transformer, 2 layers, UNITER-style) on ResNet50/Faster R-CNN features, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: ALFRED-fc (built by the authors from ALFRED): 4420 train / 642 val / 686 test samples, from 1099 image pairs and 3452 instructions; simulator-only training, zero-shot transfer to the real world
setting.observation: RGB images of target and destination candidate regions from Faster R-CNN, plus the instruction; on the real robot, head-camera (Asus Xtion Pro) images from 16 waypoints
setting.action_space: Not a navigation policy: binary classification of candidate regions. On the real robot, heuristic navigation through 16 predefined waypoints, depth-based grasp point, and rule-based placing
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (ALFRED) images for the dataset; physical WRS2020-style environment
setting.privileged: Pre-built map for navigation, predefined waypoints, and object placement on furniture assumed; the real-robot manipulation trials only executed grasping/placing when the language prediction was a true positive

numbers.extra: Trained on ALFRED-fc; mean±std over 5 runs; language comprehension accuracy
numbers.evidence: Table I: Ours (SHeFU) 83.1 ± 2.00 vs Baseline (extended TDU) 79.4 ± 2.76
Table I, Real column: SHeFU 55.9 vs baseline 52.0

numbers.eval_set_note: grasping/placing attempted only for true-positive predictions
numbers.extra: Rule-based grasping and placing; success rates on HSR

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are on the authors' ALFRED-fc dataset and a physical experiment. Metrics are classification accuracy, not SR/SPL.
results: SHeFU reaches 83.1% accuracy on ALFRED-fc versus 79.4% for the extended TDU baseline (p<0.01), and 55.9% vs 52.0% in the real world. On the robot, grasp and place success rates are 95% and 93%. Inference for a typical scene takes about 0.6 s (162 inferences) versus 26 s (6497) for the baseline.
limitations: Real-world language comprehension accuracy is low (55.9%) because of the sim-to-real gap and the zero-shot transfer.
Grasping and placing are heuristic and rule-based, and robot actions were executed only for true-positive language predictions; navigation uses a known map and predefined waypoints.
The dataset is small, with a 646-word vocabulary and image pairs with the target masked; the main error type is serious comprehension errors.
